I've been doing this for 25 years. My father farmed before me, and his father before him. I know this land. Quzhou soil is decent — we have the well, so water is not my main worry. My wife and second son work in the city now, so it's mostly me and my older son doing the field work. Eight mu is manageable for two people if we time things right.

**Wheat (this coming October through June):** I'll plant the full 8 mu in wheat as always. I use the improved variety — my neighbor switched a few years ago and his yields went up, so I followed. I put down fertilizer before planting and do a topdressing at jointing. I water before winter sets in, again at jointing, and once more at heading. That's three irrigations, sometimes four if spring is dry. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew — two times usually does it. I use the rotary tiller after the previous maize harvest to break up the stubble before seeding wheat.

**Maize (June through October):** Right after wheat harvest, I seed maize on the same 8 mu. No time to waste — the season is short. I use hybrid seed, same one I've used for years (郑单958 type). I apply fertilizer at planting and add urea when the plants are knee-high. I irrigate at planting if the soil is dry, again at tasseling, and once more at grain fill. Two or three pesticide sprays — corn borer is the main problem here. For tillage I do rotary after harvest to work the stubble back in.

I won't change much from last year. My yields have been steady. When something works, I keep doing it.
